newsitem.title: USA: Southeast U.S. banks seen as Quick & Reilly bidders.
newsitem.headline: Southeast U.S. banks seen as Quick & Reilly bidders.

text.p: Two of the largest commercial banks in the Southeast -- First Union and Barnett Banks -- are among likely bidders for Quick & Reilly Group, which put itself up for sale Monday, the New York Times said on Tuesday, citing investment bankers.
Both banks could use Quick & Reilly to help sell mutual funds, the paper said, adding that both banks declined to comment.
Quick & Reilly gave about a dozen potential buyers the chance to submit bids for it Monday, the paper said, citing people familiar with the planned sale.
According to those people, the bids were likely to value Quick & Reilly at around $1.3 billion, or 16 times its annual earnings.
Quick & Reilly hired Gleacher NatWest and Goldman, Sachs to help it with the sale, the paper said.
